decision_reason: The chosen vertex cannot serve the retained probes within the supplied static model: its six-node service-way component has no modeled outgoing adjacency to any outside native node. The metropolitan identity is retained and real-world access remains unresolved.

connector_cost.reason: The 176 m vertex gap is a diagnostic, not a traversable connector or charged driving cost.

direction_and_turns.reason: Weak-component separation prevents a modeled route in either direction; critical real-world approaches and turn permissions remain unreviewed.

legal_motor_access.reason: Outward ways carry OSM access=no tags; the service way lacks an access tag. These routing inputs are not an independent legal-access determination.

physical_connection.reason: The model proves a closed six-node component, but does not establish a physical drivable connector from the geographic origin or a real-world barrier.

same_grade.reason: Native-node connectivity is inspected, but no independent grade/crossing/entry evidence is retained.

limitations: Reject this research start for the sampled model, not Wichita eligibility or real-world accessibility. The Census origin, driving filter, source inventory and #137 gate remain unchanged; a separately reviewed urban anchor still needs independent access evidence.

reviewer.procedure: Inspect the original-point nearest-vertex choice and retained raw-way tags; reproduce bounded weak-component closure across all six exact PBFs; compare every retained probe identity against the closed component; distinguish modeled disconnection from real-world physical/legal access.

sources.provenance: Same-source raw OSM incident-way/weak-component audit, independent of the routing solver but not independent real-world access evidence.
